experiment: bullpen availability from measured reliever workload
why_retried: research_loop.py rejected a bullpen hypothesis earlier (-0.0023), but that used a crude proxy: total runs allowed in prior 3 days, which conflates starter and reliever performance. This version measures actual reliever PITCHES from pitch-level data.

sanity.note: consistent with ~140 bullpen pitches per game

signal_direction_correct.quintile_monotonic: home bullpen 3-day pitches 95 -> 244 maps to away runs 4.363 -> 4.495, monotonic
signal_direction_correct.interpretation: a more overworked bullpen does lose more, as expected

why: Same failure mode as the pitch matchup: correct sign, statistically significant raw correlation, but the effect is far too small to move a 56%-accurate classifier. A 0.035 correlation explains ~0.1% of variance.
bug_caught: First run silently produced zero rows because the arsenal pitch cache was trimmed and lacks inning_topbot/home_team. pd.read_parquet with a columns filter returned nothing rather than erroring. Fixed by switching to the pitcher_sc cache and adding an explicit schema probe that raises.
